_source: Answers drawn only from rules the platform enforces (app_config, fees.json, lifecycle.json, riders.json). If a rule changes there, change the answer here.

items.a: {city} for now. Shops deliver within {radius} km by default, and up to {maxRadius} km where a vendor chooses to cover it. We would rather start in one city properly than in fifteen badly.

items.q: How long does an order take?
items.a: Never more than {hours} hours — that ceiling is enforced by the platform on every order. Most are much quicker, because the shop is a few streets away.

A flat {base} base covers the first {freeKm} km. Beyond that, a per-km charge derived from the day's fuel price is added. Cross the shop's free-delivery threshold and the shop pays the base instead of you. The estimator on the home page works out any order to the rupee.

items.q: What happens if something goes wrong?
items.a: An order can be cancelled before pickup and anything authorised is released. Refunds are raised against the original payment with a reference you can quote, and complaints are escalated rather than closed quietly.

items.q: How much does a shop pay to sell?
items.a: Listing is free for up to 25 products. On top of the monthly plan, the platform takes {lowestFee}–3% of each sale depending on the category — the lowest is grocery.
₹{riderBase} a job, ₹{riderPerKm} a kilometre on top, and never less than ₹{riderMin} per order. The whole delivery fee reaches the rider whoever funded it, paid out weekly to their bank.

items.q: When will the apps be in the stores?
items.a: Soon. The listings are not published yet, which is why the store buttons say so instead of linking to a page that does not exist. Leave your email at the foot of the home page and we will tell you the day they land.
